name: Deerhoof
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: Rob Fisk started Deerhoof with a bass and a harmonica in San Francisco, a drummer showed up a week later, and three decades on the band has opened for Radiohead, played the Large Hadron Collider and pulled its catalog from Spotify.

eras.title: A kitchen, a week and a singer from Japan
eras.text: Rob Fisk starts a bass-and-harmonica project in San Francisco, a drummer turns up a week later, and a singer with no band experience joins the next year. Kill Rock Stars signs them off a festival set.

years.src: Wikipedia: Deerhoof · Life of the Record
years.h: Rob Fisk starts Deerhoof with a bass and a harmonica
years.p: [[Rob Fisk|0eedfcc1-da57-4c7a-99c7-7a51b31f1be0]] began Deerhoof in San Francisco in 1994 as a solo project. Drummer [[Greg Saunier|2ae4e9b4-9e8b-4a98-920d-4f3a881dac96]] joined about a week later.
years.xp:
Saunier, a 1991 Oberlin Conservatory graduate, had been drumming in a San Francisco band called Nitre Pit. When its guitarists left, he and Fisk kept the name going for the remaining shows as a stripped-down duo, per Wikipedia.

Life of the Record describes the early band rehearsing in a kitchen, with chopsticks on the drums and the bass through a practice amp.

years.h: Slim Moon catches the duo at Yoyo A Go Go
years.p: The Kill Rock Stars founder signs Deerhoof after the 1994 festival, at first for a single. The label releases their records through 2008's Offend Maggie.
years.xp: By 2003, Wikipedia notes, Deerhoof was the longest-running band on Kill Rock Stars.

years.src: Life of the Record · Wikipedia: Deerhoof
years.h: Satomi Matsuzaki lands from Japan and joins within a week
years.p: With no band experience, [[Satomi Matsuzaki|c46e7f09-6ed4-42e7-b927-86d42929bb69]] joins [[Deerhoof|11eabe0c-2638-4808-92f9-1dbd9c453429]] a week after arriving in May 1995. A week after that she is touring as its singer, opening for Caroliner.
years.xp: Life of the Record says she found the band through a Kill Rock Stars seven-inch that sounded like "crackling noise" and sometimes screaming. She has said she thought she was joining a noise band, which then turned into a rock band.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Man, the King, the Girl
years.h: The Man, the King, the Girl arrives on Kill Rock Stars
years.p: Recorded on a 4-track, it pairs twelve studio songs with five live ones, including the instrumentals "Gold on Black" and "Tiger Chain." Fisk, Matsuzaki and Saunier are the trio.
years.xp: It came out October 28, 1997, through Kill Rock Stars and 5 Rue Christine. Matsuzaki, who also draws Deerhoof's covers, sings.
play: The Man, the King, the Girl

eras.title: The founder leaves and a guitarist arrives to stay
eras.text: A keyboard player comes and goes, Fisk quits, and John Dieterich takes the guitar and is still in the band more than twenty-five years later.

years.h: Kelly Goode adds keyboards
years.p: [[Kelly Goode|f4fbb7a4-1db8-4c04-8290-7eb129f2da33]] is the first player added to the trio, and the keyboards go straight into the noise.

years.h: Xiu Xiu's Jamie Stewart hears Holdypaws and rethinks music
years.p: Self-produced and released on Kill Rock Stars. [[Xiu Xiu|8b431ac6-0806-4e4a-9b6b-1734370fa890]]'s Jamie Stewart said he had never heard anything like it and that it changed what he thought music could be.
years.xp: Critics split from the start: Pitchfork gave it 5.7 out of 10. Henry Rollins, who praised both Holdypaws and the later Green Cosmos EP, said it "gets the blood going."

years.h: Fisk and Goode leave to start 7 Year Rabbit Cycle
years.p: Founding bassist Rob Fisk and keyboardist Kelly Goode quit in 1999. [[John Dieterich|f368404c-789e-4659-a17f-d21c9a091dc1]] arrives on guitar.
years.xp:
Encyclopedia.com reports the two left together for 7 Year Rabbit Cycle, a claim I've only found in that one source.

From here Dieterich, Matsuzaki and Saunier stay put for the next quarter century, with only the second guitar chair changing hands.

eras.title: Critics start paying attention
eras.text: Dieterich and a second guitarist push the songs faster and sweeter, and Pitchfork takes notice: 8.5 for Reveille, Best New Music for Apple O'.

years.h: A trio makes Reveille and the reviews arrive
years.p: Matsuzaki plays bass, Dieterich guitar and Saunier drums on the June 2002 record that earns Deerhoof its first big reviews. Pitchfork gave it 8.5.
years.xp: It runs 33 minutes 36 seconds and came out on Kill Rock Stars and 5 Rue Christine, with a cover Matsuzaki designed. Jay and Ian Pellicci produced.

years.h: Chris Cohen sneaks in as the fourth member
years.p: Between the completion and release of Reveille, [[Chris Cohen|d06cbcab-2094-4b51-9ccf-f4af33494ef1]] becomes Deerhoof's second guitarist. Matsuzaki says he "snuck in" by coming to shows and contributing songs.
years.xp: Sources disagree on the year: Encyclopedia.com says 2001, Wikipedia says 2002. The Hemlock Tavern clip above is the four-piece two months into 2003.

yt: Live in Detroit, August 2003, full set
years.h: Pitchfork names Apple O' Best New Music
years.p: Cohen's first record as a member. Pitchfork ranked it 16th among its top albums of 2003 and 199th among the best of the decade.
years.xp: Reviewer Eric Carr called it "a fascinating trip" and praised its "intense variety and sparklingly consistent pop songwriting." Another critic said it caught the band between its noisier early days and the art-pop that followed.

years.h: A friend and former housemate draws the Milk Man cover
years.p: Ken Kagami drew the character on the sleeve of the March 2004 record. Pitchfork gave it 7.6.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com says the record made fans of Beck and Stephen Malkmus.

eras.title: Nine to five in Oakland
eras.text: A 20-track record made like a day job, a tour behind Radiohead, and the end of the four-piece.

years.h: The Green Cosmos EP goes orchestral and dancey
years.p: A mini-album on Kill Rock Stars that mixes orchestral sound with dance music. Rollins singled it out for praise.

years.src: Life of the Record · Wikipedia: The Runners Four
years.h: Everyone sings on The Runners Four, and Pitchfork gives it a 9.0
years.p: Twenty tracks, released October 11, 2005 on Kill Rock Stars, with each member taking a turn at the microphone.
years.xp:
Saunier told Life of the Record about a 13-hour stretch at the computer without leaving his chair. He also said that on a good system, after mixing it against Queens of the Stone Age, the record sounded scrawny to him.

Pitchfork later put it on its list of the 200 best albums of the 2000s.

years.big: I often feel that I missed my twenties.
q: I often feel that I missed my twenties.
years.h: Monday to Friday, nine to five, no windows
years.p: Saunier on the eight months of making The Runners Four like a day job at Soundwave, a rehearsal space in West Oakland. Chris Cohen said there was no going back to the earlier, more carefree time.
years.xp:
The band recorded Monday to Friday in a carpeted, windowless room, on a free version of Pro Tools. Guitars went through Line 6 PODS so nobody heard them in the room, and Dieterich carried an iMac on his lap from the West Oakland BART station every day.

Both Saunier and Cohen say it strained things. Cohen said it was not a success in a personal way.

years.h: Dublin night off: Thom Yorke turns up to watch Deerhoof dance
years.p: Deerhoof opened for [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]] across the US and Europe. Ed O'Brien said he wanted to steal their guitar tone, and Jonny Greenwood ran their lights at the Amsterdam soundcheck without telling them.
years.xp:
Per Drowned in Sound, Colin Greenwood apologised for missing their show at "some hole in the wall in Oxford" and then jumped around the stage imitating Matsuzaki's dancing. Phil Selway brought cupcakes to the basement dressing room in Los Angeles.

In Dublin, on a day off, Thom Yorke and Jonny Greenwood came to the band's club show and Yorke danced. Jim Warren, Radiohead's sound engineer since the early 90s, mixed the European leg because the band couldn't afford an engineer of their own.

years.h: Chris Cohen leaves, and the band is a trio again
years.p: His last work with Deerhoof is a live score for Harry Smith's Heaven and Earth Magic. The band also backs Danielson on Ships.

years.h: David Shrigley draws twelve different covers for Friend Opportunity
years.p: The January 2007 record is a trio again: Dieterich, Matsuzaki, Saunier. Pitchfork gave it 8.9.
years.xp: The A.V. Club gave it an A minus, and it peaked at No. 3 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart. It was recorded in 2006.

eras.title: Back to four, then off Kill Rock Stars
eras.text: Ed Rodriguez fills the empty guitar chair, and the band moves to Polyvinyl and starts releasing songs one website at a time.

years.h: Ed Rodriguez comes over from Gorge Trio
years.p: [[Ed Rodriguez|b88667bb-99ae-4635-a2a3-d311d59e2b8b]], who also played in [[Gorge Trio|de6800f2-ae5e-4e28-ba3b-1ee3b46b6fd9]] and XBXRX, makes Deerhoof a quartet again.

years.h: Deerhoof posts "Fresh Born" as sheet music and asks fans to record it
years.p: In summer 2008, ahead of Offend Maggie on Kill Rock Stars, the band published the song online as notation only. Metacritic scored the record 80.
years.xp: The record came out in the US on October 7, 2008, and a week later in the UK through ATP Recordings. All 14 songs are credited to Rodriguez, Saunier, Dieterich and Matsuzaki, and the band produced and mixed it themselves.

years.h: The Flaming Lips pick Deerhoof for All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: At the New York festival, [[The Flaming Lips|1f43d76f-8edf-44f6-aaf1-b65f05ad9402]] singer Wayne Coyne told Greg Saunier he was a master of spazzing out intuitively.
years.xp: Saunier says Coyne's first question backstage was how the band had written "Sirius Star."

years.h: Deerhoof and Xiu Xiu play Unknown Pleasures start to finish
years.p: Joy Division's whole record, with [[Xiu Xiu|8b431ac6-0806-4e4a-9b6b-1734370fa890]], at Donaufestival in Austria and on the Williamsburg waterfront in Brooklyn.

yt: "Panda Panda Panda", Liquid Room, Tokyo, December 2011
years.h: Deerhoof vs. Evil leaks out one website at a time
years.p: "The Merry Barracks" premiered on Pitchfork on October 8, 2010. The other tracks followed on different sites before Polyvinyl Records released the full album.
years.xp:
The album went out in waves: Japan on January 6 (P-Vine), the UK on January 24 (ATP), the US on January 25 (Polyvinyl) and New Zealand on January 30 (Flying Nun). The band produced it themselves, and Saunier mixed and mastered it.

Metacritic scored it 77; AllMusic gave it 4 of 5.

years.h: Breakup Song is a flexi-book
years.p: Released on Polyvinyl and Joyful Noise Recordings, it lets listeners flip from song to song like pages in a storybook.
years.xp: The band wrote it because they felt breakup songs are usually too sad. That October they put out the single "Sexy, but Sparkly" with Chris Shaw, their first time working with an outside producer.

years.h: A live Ramones cover turns into "Exit Only"
years.p: The lead single from La Isla Bonita grew out of Deerhoof's live version of "Pinhead." The record was made at guitarist Ed Rodriguez's home.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the demos were cut over a week at Rodriguez's Oregon home with producer Nick Sylvester, and that "Exit Only" came out as the first single on August 20, 2014. Matsuzaki told Vice they recorded in Ed's basement over ten days in a really small room.

eras.title: The Large Hadron Collider, then the exit
eras.text: Deerhoof plays CERN, trails the Red Hot Chili Peppers across northern Europe, and in 2025 takes its catalog off Spotify.

yt: Ex/Noise/CERN: Deerhoof vs. the Large Hadron Collider
years.h: Deerhoof plays the Large Hadron Collider
years.p: In August 2015 the band becomes the first act invited to perform improvisational, site-specific noise music at CERN.
years.xp: CERN's film of the visit became one of the ten most-watched videos the lab has made. Physicist James Beacham said musical curiosity is like scientific curiosity, and that Deerhoof has inspired him as much as Einstein.

years.h: The Magic is their first No. 1 on CMJ
years.p: It blends glam metal, punk and noise, and covers The Ink Spots' "I Don't Want to Set the World on Fire."

years.h: Deerhoof follows the Red Hot Chili Peppers' trucks in a Prius
years.p: In November 2016 the band opens arenas across northern Europe, trailing the Chili Peppers' buses in a Prius minivan.
years.xp: Saunier told Stereogum: "You have not experienced acoustical challenges until you've tried to play a 20,000-seat indoor arena." Reverb in a room that size, he said, turns a snare hit to mud.

years.cap: Deerhoof at Haldern Pop Festival, Germany
years.h: Deerhoof calls in friends for a protest record
years.p: Mountain Moves features Awkwafina, Jenn Wasner, Juana Molina and Lætitia Sadier. Early Bandcamp sales benefited the Emergent Fund.
years.xp: The band premiered it on Bandcamp on August 28, 2017, and Joyful Noise Recordings released it September 8. Of its 15 tracks, three are covers: Violeta Parra's "Gracias a la Vida," the Staple Singers' "Freedom Highway" and Bob Marley's "Small Axe."

years.h: Future Teenage Cave Artists tells a story
years.p: Wikipedia calls the May 2020 record the band's first overt concept album.

years.h: Miracle-Level is sung entirely in Japanese
years.p: Recorded June 25 to July 3, 2022 at No Fun Club in Winnipeg. Pitchfork gave it 7.9.
years.xp:
It's the band's first record with every lyric in Japanese, and its first made with an outside engineer: Mike Bridavsky recorded, mixed and mastered at Russian Recording in Bloomington, Indiana. Kunie Sugiura made the cover, and the First Regiment of the Zumiko Sakumura Brass Band plays horns.

Metacritic scored it 83.

years.src: Wikipedia: Noble and Godlike in Ruin
years.h: Noble and Godlike in Ruin stitches four faces into "Deerhoofstein"
years.p: Saunier calls the April 2025 record the band's low-budget DIY Frankenstein. Its cover sews the four members' faces together.
years.xp: The title comes from Mary Shelley's Frankenstein. Saunier describes the album as a "sensitive, spurned, intelligent, dehumanized creature made out of people." Saul Williams raps on "Under Rats," and Pitchfork gave it 7.2.

years.big: We don't want our music killing people.
q: We don't want our music killing people.
years.h: Deerhoof leaves Spotify
years.p: The band said it would pull its catalog over CEO Daniel Ek's investment in Helsing, a German defense AI company.
years.xp:
MusicRadar reported the band said Spotify "only pays a pittance anyway" and that it earns more from touring than streaming. It also called Spotify a "data-mining scam," while acknowledging that other artists depend on the platform for real income.

The announcement landed in the weeks after Noble and Godlike in Ruin came out. Wikipedia dates it June 30, 2025; MusicRadar ran it July 2.
